placements.why: This is the first envelope in this repo to carry calibration-domain content — an instrument's tuned figure checked against reference plates and confirmed to hold across the observing band. Nothing in the supplied (empty) strata covers this, and the org's known top-level taxonomy names 'Calibration' as exactly this category, so it is minted standalone rather than forced under any other stratum.
placements.title: Observatory instrument calibration as a distinct organizational stratum
placements.frame: Does this envelope's content concern verifying, holding, or documenting an instrument's calibration state against reference standards?

placements.title: Calibration figures reported as verified, reference-grounded states, not bare specs
placements.frame: When an instrument's calibration value is reported, was it checked against a reference standard and shown to hold across conditions, or only declared?
placements.why: src-1 narrates the calibration as settled and verified ('is now calibrated ... We verified the calibration ... it holds across the full observing band'); src-2 and src-3 restate the identical content in flat field-label form ('**Instrument**: Kestrelwood spectrograph', '**Calibration**: 88.4 MHz, verified against June reference plates'). All three converge on the same directional theme — calibration as a checked, evidence-grounded state rather than a raw number — which is a subject future calibration envelopes will keep feeding (other instruments, other reference sets), not a one-time fact. The specific figure (88.4 MHz) and the specific reference set (June plates) are facts supporting this leaf, not leaves themselves.
